title: The Wedding WhatsApp Disaster
synopsis: A Kerala wedding group chat spirals into chaos when its enthusiastic administrator schedules everything twice.

chapters.title: Welcome to the Group
paragraphs: When cousin Binu was made administrator of the family wedding group, he announced that communication would be professional. Within an hour he had created twelve subgroups, a dress-code spreadsheet and a poll about whether the welcome drink should be lime juice or pineapple juice.
Grandmother joined the wrong subgroup and voted for fish curry. Nobody had the courage to remove her vote, so fish curry briefly led the drinks poll.

chapters.title: The Voice Note
paragraphs: Uncle Suresh sent a six-minute voice note about parking arrangements. Binu summarized it as 'All cars to north gate.' Unfortunately, the venue had no north gate. The voice note had actually said that cars should avoid the north side because of construction.

By evening, three relatives had shared the incorrect instruction with people who were not even attending the wedding. Binu created a new subgroup called Parking Clarification. Grandmother posted another fish curry suggestion.

chapters.title: The Duplicate Invitation
paragraphs: Binu scheduled a reminder message for the ceremony, then accidentally scheduled it again in a different time zone. Half the guests believed the wedding began at seven in the morning, the other half at seven at night.

The bride, Diya, asked everyone to stop forwarding screenshots and read the printed invitation. Binu insisted that digital systems were more reliable, right before his phone announced that the wedding was happening yesterday.

chapters.title: Operation Banana Leaf
paragraphs: A caterer asked for the final guest count. Binu's spreadsheet showed 812 people, although only 260 had been invited. It turned out he had counted every reaction emoji as a separate guest.

Diya's brother corrected the list by calling each family directly. The caterer thanked him and ordered enough banana leaves for the real number. Binu renamed the spreadsheet 'Final Final Absolutely Final v7'.

chapters.title: The Actual Wedding
paragraphs: On the morning of the wedding, Binu's phone battery died. He panicked until he noticed that the flower decorators, musicians and caterers were already working from a simple printed schedule prepared by Diya.
The ceremony began on time. Grandmother greeted guests, directed them to their seats and made sure nobody missed lunch. For once, nobody needed a notification.

chapters.title: One Last Message
paragraphs: After the wedding, Binu charged his phone and discovered 1,406 unread messages. The newest was from Grandmother: 'Good wedding. Fish curry excellent.'

Binu closed every subgroup except one. He renamed it 'Family' and posted a single photograph of the newlyweds. Nobody replied for ten peaceful minutes. Then Uncle Suresh sent a voice note about parking.
